stories.article_text_excerpt: The mass influx of migrants into Ceuta over the summer has placed a controversial migration measure on EU ministers’ agenda. In July, the sudden arrival of more than 70,000 migrants to the small Spanish North African territory triggered chaos, just as the EU was rolling out sweeping migration reforms to secure its external borders. Several countries argue that it should be possible to temporarily suspend asylum applications in crises of this scale under a new emergency procedure. “If 70,000 people — mostly young men— arrive in a single day, then that obviously has nothing to do with asylum,” Austria’s Interior Minister Gerhard Karner said Thursday. “And if that’s the case, then the existing regulations aren’t sufficient to handle it.” Advertisement Advertisement Earlier this week, Migration Commissioner Magnus Brunner presented plans to prevent and address sudden mass arrivals on the bloc’s borders that may be engineered and weaponized by other countries, including a ramped-up role for border agency Frontex. The blueprint also included a European emergency response framework, which Commission President Ursula von der Leyen had included in her State of the Union address last month.

First, the Gulf of Mexico became the Gulf of America — in US federal documents, if not globally. Then Lake Ontario became Lake America. Now he wants to rebrand the defining technology of our time: artificial intelligence (AI). Earlier this month, the US president claimed on his Truth Social platform that the term artificial intelligence is "inaccurate" and "ineloquent." He said "superior," "extreme," or "supreme" intelligence were better alternatives. In a three-day social media poll, Trump fans chose "Super Intelligence" (SI) by about 65% to 35% (for Superior Intelligence), allowing him to announce at the United Nations General Assembly last week that US federal documents would use his new term going forward.
